Michael Moore is currently one of the most in demand bassists in jazz. He was born in 1945 in Glen Este, Ohio, and started on the acoustic bass at the age of 15. Michael attended the Cincinnati Conservatory and honed his skills with guitarist Cal Collins at the Playboy Club of Cincinnati. After a 1966 tour with Woody Herman he settled in New York and played with an impressive group of jazz artists. Benny Goodman, Marian McPartland, Chet Baker, Herb Ellis, and numerous others have benefited from his virtuosity, and he continues to record and tour with the top jazz musicians in the field. One of his latest recordings is with Arbors artist Rebecca Kilgore, entitled “I Saw Stars.”
Michael was interviewed on September 12, 1997 at the Allegheny Jazz Party in Chautauqua, New York by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
